## Brazilian public data, ready to check

I work with Brazilian public data and build tools that deliver it ready for
analysis: every number comes with its source and the path back to it, because a
number without provenance cannot support an argument.

### MCP servers for AI assistants

Servers that give Claude, ChatGPT and other assistants live access to official
data: IBGE (SIDRA, Census, municipalities), the Central Bank of Brazil (SGS time
series, Focus market expectations, PTAX exchange rates), the Brazilian Senate
(votes, bills, parliamentary expenses), medical terminologies (ICD-10, ICD-11,
LOINC) and the international databases of the ILO and UNESCO. Nothing to
install: point any MCP client at the server's address. [See the servers →](/tools/)

### R packages

Packages that download, read and tidy official data straight into R: education
(INEP), public health (DATASUS, PNS, VIGITEL), listed companies and funds (CVM)
and the Brazilian Senate. Two of them are on CRAN. [See the packages →](/packages/)

### Blog

Tutorials and analyses built on the data these tools serve: finding the right
SIDRA table, the pitfalls of Central Bank time series, and the move from ICD-10
to ICD-11 in Brazil's public health system. [Read the blog →](/blog/)

### A citable dataset

The participation layer of the Brazilian Senate's e-Cidadania portal, versioned,
with a DOI on Zenodo and field-by-field provenance: the layer no legislative data
package covered. [Learn more →](/about.html)
